title: San Francisco Keeps Its Flock Cameras, With New Restrictions | KQED
summary: San Francisco Mayor Daniel Lurie announced new restrictions on the city's Flock ALPR system, including a 30-day data access limit, incident-number justification for searches, monthly SFPD reviews, and independent audits by the Department of Police Accountability. Officials also pledged to pursue state legislation criminalizing misuse of ALPR data, following revelations that SFPD data was improperly accessed by federal and out-of-state agencies and a San José officer was fired for misuse.

key_quotes.quote: Every active search will have to be connected to a specific incident number. The officer will have to state the reason for the search and the system will record who conducted it.
In June, the SFPD revealed that their Automated License Plate Reader, or ALPR, data had been improperly accessed hundreds of times by out-of-state and federal agencies.
This technology keeps San Franciscans safe, and we will not go back to a time where people can break into cars, rob businesses or commit serious crime and expect to get away with it.
